Marta: heads-up: CI perf run shows a 22% P50 regression on chat-workload B when KV cache hit rate > 70%. Attached profile points at kernel selector bouncing to SDPA fallback for a subset of batches.

Omar: can you paste the sample trace?

Marta: sure — snippet from perf-bot: 
```
perf-bot: trace 1943210000: model=redwood-chat-xl seq=1024 batch=4 head_dim=48 causal=true kv_cache_hit=0.78
selected_kernel: flash_v3 (fastpath) -> fallback sdpa_v2_slowpath (reason: head_dim alignment miss + seqlen>512)
latency_tokens: 11.8ms -> 15.2ms
```

Jen: interesting — head_dim=48 used to be fine. looks like flash_v3 autotuner is mis-evaluating microbench for causal path when kv_cache warmup reduces effective sequence patterns.

Kai: repro'd locally w/ my microbatcher. If KV cache is warm and prefix lengths vary across batch, the autotuner probes average seqlen incorrectly and chooses a kernel optimized for longer contiguous KV access that accidentally thrashes L2.

Omar: can you share the quick repro command?

Kai: run this:
```
python -m perf_runner --model r-chat-xl --batch 4 --seqlens 512,1024,384,1024 --head_dim 48 --causal True --kv_warmup 1
```

Marta: stacktrace shows selector compare uses (avg_seqlen, head_dim, causal) but ignores kv_cache_hit_rate. I think we need to factor in kv cache hit ratio into the kernel scoring.

Jen: +1. Also we should special-case odd head dims (48) for flash_v3 causal: either pad head_dim to multiple-of-32 in kernel pick, or penalize flash_v3 score when head_dim % 16 !=0.

Omar: penalty approach seems less invasive. quick patch idea: add a cost multiplier when head_dim % 16 != 0 OR kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.6 and avg_seqlen > 512. I sketched a diff: 
```
--- a/runtime/kernel_selector.cpp
+++ b/runtime/kernel_selector.cpp
@@
- score = microbench_ms(avg_seqlen, head_dim, kernel);
+ score = microbench_ms(avg_seqlen, head_dim, kernel);
+ if ((head_dim % 16) != 0) score *= 1.12; // account for shuffle/pad overhead
+ if (kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.6 && avg_seqlen > 512) score *= 1.08; // prefer kernels tuned for fragmented KV
```

Kai: small number constants but ok as a stopgap. We should add a regression test that synthesizes the mixed-prefix batch and asserts kernel choice stays on flash_v2 or penalized-v3 path.

perf-bot: perf test queued: perf/regressions/1943210000-kernelpicker. Expect ~10–15m.

Marta: also: we saw odd interaction where padding overhead improved latency once we force padded head_dim=64. So a long-term fix might be to teach runtime to consider runtime-padding fallback (lazy pad to 64 when cheap).

Jen: agree. Action items: (1) Omar will push penalty patch + unit test, (2) Kai will add mixed-prefix microbenchmark and run perf workloads, (3) Marta will log an RFC for runtime-padding heuristics.

Omar: i'll open a PR in a bit. PR title: "kernel-selector: penalize flash_v3 for unaligned head_dim and high-kv-warmup". cc: @Jen @Kai

Marta: thanks. FYI if perf-bot shows no regression after patch we can roll to canary. If still failing we consider automatic pad-to-64 for head_dim<64 when causal and kv_cache_hit>0.6.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout to eng-dedicated-1 starting in 30m (if tests pass). :rocket:

Kai: one more note — update the autotuner to run microprobes across a vector of kv_cache_hit_rate buckets (0.0, 0.5, 0.9) so we don't miss these cases. I can prototype in the tuner next week.

Jen: thanks all. I'll add the regression case to the nightly perf suite.

Marta: closing loop here once PR lands. :thumbsup:
